notes.japanese: いつか暗くなった戸の外に、激しい雨風の音がする、嵐だ。
notes.problem: The modifier dangles so the door seems to have grown dark, and the trailing apposition reads as a label rather than prose.
notes.span: Outside the door, grown dark at some point, the sound of violent rain and wind could be heard, a storm.
notes.suggestion: Outside the door, which had grown dark at some point, violent rain and wind could be heard: a storm.
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; faithful reader to confirm that at some point belongs to darkening, not to hearing.

notes.japanese: しかし男の濃い眉毛の陰のくぼんだ優しさうな瞳には、だるさうな疲れの色が見えてゐた。そして女の濃い髪のいろや、細やかな肩のあたりには、なほ打沈んだやうな深い疲れと、まどろむやうな安らかさとが見えてゐた。
notes.problem: Two passive catalogue sentences with un-English prepositions have to be read twice and never become a seen couple.
notes.span: But in the man's sunken, gentle-looking eyes in the shadow of his thick eyebrows a dull colour of weariness could be seen. And in the colour of the woman's thick hair and about her slight shoulders a still more sunken deep weariness and a drowsy restfulness could be seen.
notes.suggestion: But in the man's sunken, gentle eyes in the shadow of his thick eyebrows there was a dull cast of weariness. And in the woman's thick hair and about her slight shoulders there was an even deeper, sunken weariness and a drowsy restfulness.
notes.sureness: Very sure as English; keeping weariness and restfulness repeated as the house requires would settle it.

notes.japanese: そして、彼等は黙って微笑しながら、その子供のすべてに瞳を注いだ。
notes.problem: All their eyes is not idiomatic English and sounds like a dictionary plural rather than people looking.
notes.span: And silently smiling, they turned all their eyes upon the child.
notes.suggestion: And silently smiling, they fixed all their gaze upon the child.
notes.sureness: Very sure; any native reader stumbles on all their eyes, faithful reader to confirm the totality is kept.

notes.japanese: 大きな茶碗をテーブルの下から探すやうにしてとると、彼女の手に渡した。
notes.problem: Her hand has no clear owner after a paragraph about father and child, and put it into her hand is unidiomatic.
notes.span: he took a large bowl from under the table as if feeling for it and put it into her hand.
notes.suggestion: he felt under the table for a large bowl and put it in the child's hand.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure about into versus in; unsure who her is, and what would settle it is the faithful note on p7 彼女.

notes.japanese: どうにも仕方がない程可愛いといふやうな様子で
notes.problem: Loved it beyond all help dehumanises the baby to it and the idiom does not exist in English, breaking the tenderness.
notes.span: looking for all the world as if she loved it beyond all help
notes.suggestion: looking for all the world as if she loved the child helplessly
notes.sureness: Very sure it stops an English reader; faithful reader to confirm child stays plain and no grander tenderness is added.

notes.japanese: そのすきに彼は、あわたゞしく大きな口を開けた、彼は彼自身の口のなかに御飯を押し込んだ。
notes.problem: The dangling participle detaches the wide mouth from the father and reads comic on first pass.
notes.span: In the gaps, hurriedly opening a wide mouth, he pushed rice into his own mouth.
notes.suggestion: In the gaps between, he hurriedly opened his mouth wide and pushed rice into it.
notes.sureness: Very sure; punctuation alone cannot save the dangler.

notes.japanese: そしてジャガ芋の無味な、かゝはりのない冷やかな不味さが、彼女に静かな淋しい遠くはなれた心を与へた。
notes.problem: Flavourless plus tastelessness is redundant and detached plus far-removed for a heart is dictionary English, not plain prose.
notes.span: And the flavourless, detached, cold tastelessness of the potato gave her a quiet, lonely, far-removed heart.
notes.suggestion: And the cold, flavourless, indifferent tastelessness of the potato gave her a quiet, lonely, far-away heart.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure the pile needs thinning but the plain repeated words quiet, lonely, far must stay; desk to weigh against faithful literalism.

notes.japanese: 静かに涙にみちた日のことや、物質の為めに脅かされ恐れてすごした日々や、病の為めに悲しみ苦しんだその日その日のこと
notes.problem: Days spent threatened and afraid is ungrammatical and the last clause leaves unclear who grieved, so the list cannot pool as intended.
notes.span: and the days spent threatened and afraid for material things, and each and every day grieved and suffered through illness.
notes.suggestion: and the days lived threatened and afraid over material things, and each single day grieved and suffered through in illness.
notes.sureness: Very sure it must be reparsed to be read at all; faithful reader to confirm agency is left soft as in Japanese.

notes.japanese: また瞳の底を通して遠く未来に、淋しい安らかさを持って、その絵が見えるのであった。
notes.problem: A pile of passives and prepositional phrases buries the vision just where the prose should pool and carry.
notes.span: And through the bottom of her eyes, far off in the future, with a lonely restfulness, that picture could be seen.
notes.suggestion: And through the bottom of her eyes that picture could be seen, far off in the future, in a lonely restfulness.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure reordering helps English without adding lyricism; what would settle it is hearing whether the strangeness survives.

notes.japanese: と男にも思出して、種々のことを、結婚前の楽しかったことまでも、思出して下さいと云ふやうに云った。
notes.problem: The speech tag stutters to remember, to remember and runs three infinitives together in a machine habit no writer would sign.
notes.span: as if asking him too to remember, to remember all kinds of things, even the happy things from before their marriage.
notes.suggestion: as if asking him too to remember — all kinds of things, even the happy things from before their marriage.
notes.sureness: Very sure as English rhythm; faithful reader to confirm no softness about who remembers is lost.

notes.japanese: 一日々々いろいろなことに疲らされなやまされ苦しまされても、二年はもう過ぎたんだからな。
notes.problem: Triple passive plus are past already is stiff for what should be rough-edged warm speech and has to be read twice.
notes.span: Though day by day we are wearied and troubled and made to suffer by one thing and another, two years are past already.
notes.suggestion: Though day by day one thing and another wears us and troubles us and makes us suffer, two years are gone already.
notes.sureness: Fairly sure the active carries the voice better in English; what would settle it is the faithful check that weariness, trouble, suffering stay as the same repeated nouns.

notes.japanese: 彼女は、すぐに嬉しさうに、『坊や。』と大きな声を出した、子供はそれと同時に大きな叫声を上げて、母親の顔を見ながら、『うまうまうまうま。』とスプーンをテーブルにたゝきつけた。
notes.problem: She has no anchor after the man looked, and the babble tacked after a comma reads as if it were what the cry said rather than simultaneous noise.
notes.span: At once she called out joyfully, "Baby." At the same moment the child gave a loud cry, looking at her mother's face, and banged the spoon down on the table, "uma-uma-uma-uma."
notes.suggestion: At once the mother called out joyfully, Baby. At the same moment the child, looking at her mother's face, gave a loud cry and banged the spoon down on the table: uma-uma-uma-uma.
notes.sureness: Very sure the pronoun and punctuation block reading; faithful reader to settle Baby versus period usage and whether mother must stay she.

data.say: Domestic opening reads as literal draft with passive catalogues, danglers and pronoun tangles that block tenderness; vision mostly lives where diction stays plain.
